scope: Original-circuit complementary count: sum over heavy i of (|S_i|-1) + number of light targets of size>=2 + |Y| <= C.size, under |Y|>=2. The exact weighted sum decomposes as B_heavy+L_nontrivial+Q_light+P, yielding the 997 sufficient criterion Q_light<=R+|Y|+(m-P). The unrestricted 997 inequality remains open.
math_audit: Heavy OR charges are pairwise disjoint and false on Y in the constant-false NOT replacement.
Large light output gates are distinct valid gates and true on Y, so they avoid every heavy charge.
Minterm branches are empty-singleton-support ANDs true on Y at or before the valid NOT input u, and u lies before the NOT gate z.
A large light output cannot be a prefix branch: if it were before z, same-index prefix preservation would identify its replacement singleton support with the original target of size at least two.
The replacement z has empty sample support, so no heavy charge uses it. In the original circuit z is true at zero, so no target OR output uses it. Prefix branches avoid it by order.
The minterm count therefore adds |Y|-1 branches and the unused NOT gate to the heavy/light union.
The finite sum decomposition and m-P slack preserve arbitrary empty and singleton targets, including repeated singleton targets.
The exact same refundGates definition is used, with the checked equality to the posted predicate inherited from RefundCount.
